title: The Core of LLM Applications: Grounding

scenes.line1: Is your LLM grounded or just guessing?
scenes.line2: How do you make it reliable?
scenes.say: Is your language model actually answering from facts, or just making things up? How do you make its answers reliable?

scenes.label: Prompt
scenes.sub: Your prompt shapes what the model outputs.
scenes.say: It all starts with your prompt. The way you ask shapes the answer you get.
But the real magic is grounding. You prompt the model, use embeddings to find relevant info, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation brings in the facts.
If you skip grounding, the model just guesses and can hallucinate. With grounding, it cites sources and reduces errors.

scenes.question: Does RAG stop all hallucinations?
scenes.right: No, RAG helps but you still need filters and checks.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: does retrieval always guarantee truth? Nope. RAG helps, but you still need filters and checks.
